description: The rules of the operational-notice contract, as DATA: AUB's Go store and read route, the JavaScript reference implementation every client runs (AUP, AUG, AUCOM's page) and the operator CLI in auto-pigeon-tools all read these numbers rather than restating them.

poll.notes: A client fetches at start-up and then every `poll_after_seconds` the server published, clamped to [min_seconds, max_seconds], with ±`jitter_fraction` of random spread (the result is clamped back into the window) so a fleet of clients does not synchronise. After a failure it backs off exponentially from `backoff_base_seconds` to `backoff_max_seconds`, again with jitter. One request is in flight at a time, and every repeat is conditional (If-None-Match).

notes: Notices are PLAIN TEXT. A client renders them as text nodes, never as HTML or Markdown, so markup is inert wherever it is shown. The store additionally REFUSES text that looks like markup (`refused_patterns`), so an operator is told at write time rather than a user seeing angle brackets later; links, if ever needed, are a new schema version.
`removed_ranges` are code points a client deletes and the store refuses: C0/C1 controls (except LF in a body), bidi overrides and isolates, zero-width characters and the byte-order mark.

telemetry.notes: The ONLY events a client may emit about notices. Low cardinality by construction: no notice id, title, body, account or dismissal choice.

operator_time.notes: An operator may type a local wall-clock time in an IANA REGION zone (Area/Location, e.g. Europe/Copenhagen) or UTC. Abbreviations such as CET, CEST or EST5EDT are refused: `CET` is not a year-round synonym for Copenhagen, and a tool that accepted it would be wrong for half the year. A nonexistent local time (spring-forward gap) is refused; an ambiguous one (autumn fall-back) is refused unless the operator chooses fold 0 (the first, summer-time occurrence) or fold 1 (the second). The resulting UTC instant is always shown back.
